Wang Lung (to O-lan): "Now, my poor wife, there is no need to keep the two small pearls any longer. Give them to me that I may buy the gold pin and wear it to the tea shop and show it to my sweetheart."

O-lan (to Wang Lung): "I have not kept them for my own sake, or for yours, but for the daughters---for the daughters when they are old enough to marry. I would give them the two small pearls if I were sure that they would keep them and not sell them for a bowl of rice or a catty of coal. But I am afraid to give them to you because when you have bought the gold pin you will sell them and take the money to buy yourself a new coat or new shoes."

Wang Lung (to O-lan): "How can I wear the gold pin and show it to my sweetheart without the two small white pearls? Now, my poor wife, I will ask you once more. Give them to me that I may buy the pin and wear it to the tea shop and show it to my sweetheart."
[says] (to Wang Lung) O-lan expresses concern about her daughters' future and her desire to secure their well-being.
[says] Wang Lung asks O-lan again, then suddenly leaves.
O-lan (to Wang Lung): "Give me the two small pearls and I will give them to the girls when they are married and it is time. Now---now---"

wang_lung.raw: I want O-lan's attention and affection, but I'm afraid if I show her kindness, she'll think I've forgotten Lotus, my new love.
